package_info.package_name: Injected JavaScript Magecart skimmer (Warner Music Group online store)
package_info.package_manager: N/A (injected client-side JavaScript, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malicious code injected directly into production site, not versioned)
package_info.why_malicious: The injected JavaScript code acts as a Magecart-style web skimmer, intercepting sensitive customer data (including payment and personal information) from checkout forms on the Warner Music Group online store and exfiltrating it to an attacker-controlled domain. This enables large-scale theft of customer data directly from the browser during legitimate transactions.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user submits a form in the browser
execution_context.file_location: Injected <script> tag or inline JavaScript within compromised Warner Music Group online store checkout pages
required_permissions: Access to DOM (to hook form submission events and read form data)
Network access (to send outbound HTTPS requests to external domains)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user submits a form, the code hooks into the form submission event, collects all form data (including payment and personal information), and sends this data via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive customer information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts all form submissions and exfiltrates the complete form data to an external, non-legitimate domain, which is a hallmark of Magecart-style web skimming attacks. The use of a hardcoded, untrusted endpoint for data exfiltration is highly indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce JavaScript should never transmit sensitive checkout or payment form data to unknown or undocumented third-party domains. All data handling should be restricted to trusted payment processors or the store's own backend, and code should not be injected or obfuscated.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment processing scripts may collect form data, but only to well-known, documented, and trusted endpoints (such as Stripe or PayPal). These scripts are typically reviewed, not injected, and their network destinations are transparent and verifiable.
key_indicators: Hooks into global form submission events using document.addEventListener('submit', ...)
Reads and serializes all form data via FormData API
Sends outbound HTTPS POST requests to a hardcoded, attacker-controlled domain not associated with the legitimate store
Presence of injected or obfuscated JavaScript code not present in the original site source
Script appears in unexpected locations (e.g., inline in checkout pages or as a new/modified external script)

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to the Warner Music Group online store infrastructure and injects malicious JavaScript code into the checkout or payment pages.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript is loaded and executed in the browsers of customers visiting the compromised store.

attack_chain.action: The injected JavaScript hooks into form submission events, collects all data entered by the user (including payment and personal information), and prepares it for exfiltration.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive customer data is captured in the browser before legitimate processing.

attack_chain.action: The malicious code sends the captured form data via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltrated customer data is received by the attacker, enabling theft of personal and financial information for further exploitation or sale.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code that globally hooks into form submission events (e.g., document.addEventListener('submit', ...))
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with the legitimate e-commerce platform, especially during checkout or payment form submission
Presence of injected, obfuscated, or newly added JavaScript code in checkout or payment pages that is not part of the original site source
file_indicators: Unexpected <script> tags or inline JavaScript blocks in checkout or payment pages
New or modified external JavaScript files in web server directories (e.g., /js/, /assets/) that are not part of the official site deployment
References to external JavaScript files from suspicious or unrecognized domains
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests from client browsers to hardcoded, attacker-controlled domains (e.g., https://malicious-domain.com/collect) during checkout or form submission
Frequent small POST requests containing form-encoded or multipart data to unknown domains during the checkout process
DNS lookups or connections to domains not present in the legitimate store's allowlist
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor e-commerce site source code for unauthorized changes, especially new or modified JavaScript in checkout/payment pages. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unexpected <script> tags or external script references. Deploy web application firewalls (WAFs) and network monitoring to detect and block outbound POST requests to untrusted domains. Regularly audit network traffic for suspicious destinations and inspect browser-side code for evidence of form data interception and exfiltration.
